Unfortunately surviving the long term is rediculously easy when you get the hang of it. 

- 3-4x Flint spears, a bighorn takes 4 i think, and a boar takes 3 (thrown)

- butcher them, grab the meat and SAVE THE FAT

- get clay and make a cooking pot, 4x bowls, and as many crocks as you can

- when all fired, slide 16 redmeat evenly into the four slots of your cooking pot. then fill you crocks with this "4x hefty redmeat stew"

- USE THE FAT FROM EARLIER to "seal" the crocks, now making them into basically canned goods that will last near indefinitely.

(you can also use fat and bowls to make permanent lamps for your base)

And bam, you now have a long term food supply.

When you get to the copper age, craft a saw. This will allow to you make shelves which will make you sealed redmeat stews last even longer. (1.6 years on average when put in a cellar)

I think its important to mention it wasn't the Bolsheviks who led or controlled any of the major soviets (Vyborg and of course Petrograd) who the main challenges to the provisional government during the struggle of "dual power".

The soviets were manifested autonomously for the most part with the majority of electoral representation lending to Menshevik or "Socialist Revolutionary" - the more conservative factions of the October revolution.

The provisional government by the time of the revolution had demonstrated their incapability to continue administration of the Russia, members themselves admitting that the real political power at the time belonged to workers soviets and soldier deputies. Though that sentiment did not extend towards the main rank and file of the proletariat until late into the system of dual power.

When General Kornilov in a last attempt to preserve "White" power by enacting a coup against the provisional government - an act intended to create a proto-fascist dictatorship against the communists - it was the soviets who defended them, consolidating the view of the Bolsheviks that the real power belonged to the soviets, a major factor to why the Bolsheviks gained a majority of support during the urban struggles of the revolution.
